distinguishing_features: Uses an active time-varying electrostatic field to supplement normal force rather than merely monitoring drive-motor current as a proxy
Actuates a physical adhesion force (Coulombic attraction between electrodes and belt) instead of inferring a wear/slip precursor from telemetry
Adds new hardware (HV electrode array, 5 kV converter) to modulate friction dynamically, rather than exploiting only already-recorded signals
Targets slip prevention on ultra-smooth glossy boards via electrostatic normal-force augmentation, a failure mode none of the cited monitoring references address
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Prevent belt slip against an ultra-smooth board at high line speed where mechanical friction coefficient alone is insufficient.
parsed.viable_reason: The Coulombic force estimate (about 1.1 N at 5 kV, 1 mm gap) is physically sound and testable via encoder slip measurement, though the ~10% normal-force contribution is modest.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Applying a dynamically modulated electrostatic field to augment friction via Coulombic normal force is a genuine mechanism departure; none of the monitoring-only prior art suggests active adhesion actuation, and it is not a routine parameter tweak of that art.
